title_ar: الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو يحاضر في جامع الهدى بمقاطعة لكصر عن "استغلال الوقت"
title_en: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Lectures at the al-Huda Mosque in the Ksar District on "Making Use of Time"
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة - بجامع الهدى بمقاطعة لكصر وسط العاصمة انواكشوط - بعنوان: استغلال الوقت في حياة المسلم، وذلك بعد صلاة المغرب من مساء يوم أمس الأحد، حضرها جمهور غفير من طلاب العلم ورجال الدعوة، وكان للنساء حضور معتبر.

وقد تطرق الشيخ في محاضرته لقيمة الوقت في حياة المسلم وكيف يستغل المسلم وقته الثمين بانسجام مع التكاليف الكثيرة، وقد وضع الشيخ - في حديثه - لذلك تخطيطا وتنظيما يساعد الإنسان على ترشيد وقته وصرفه في الصالح والنافع، مسترشدا في ذلك بفقه الأولويات والموازنة بين المصالح.

وقد تطرقت المحاضرة لمواضيع مهمة فقهية وفكرية ووعظية، نذكر منها تلخيصا مايلي:

• الوقت رأس المال، ولا يمكن للإنسان أن يحرز ربحا بفوات رأس المال.

• عظَّم القرآن من شأن الوقت فأقسم سبحانه وتعالى في أكثر من سورة بمواقيت زمانية؛ فأقسم بالشمس والقمر وتعاقبهما وبالضحي وبالليل وبالنهار.. وكل هذا تنبيه إلى أهمية الوقت وعظمته.

• وقت الإنسان هو عمره وجعله الله مجهولا بالنسبة إليه لحكمة بليغة لا يدركها إلا أصحاب العقول النيِّرة.

• الوقت حجة على الإنسان فعليه أن يبادر إلى استغلاله أمثل استغلال، وقد قال الحسن بن أبي الحسن رحمه الله: " إن عمرا ضيع أوله لجدير أن يحفظ آخره"

• بقية العمر ثمنها كثير لأنها هي التي بها يتدارك الإنسان ما فات، وقد قال محمد عالي بن عبد الودود رحمه الله تعالى:

بقية العمر عـندي مالها ثمن **** ولو غداً غير محبوب من الـزمن

يستدرك المرء فيها كل فائتة **** من الزمان ويمحو السوء بالحسن.

• الإنسان يحتاج في استغلال وقته أمثل استغلال إلى ترتيب الأولويات والتفكير في أمثلها، ويوقف تصرفه في الأمور حتى يعلم حكم الله في ما سيفعله. ثم بعد ذلك يبادر إلى امتثال الواجب منه فإذا أكمل الواجب بادر إلى ما يتمم الواجب من السنن والمندوبات، فإذا وصل إلى درجة المباحات فلا بد من أن يزن الأمور بميزان آخر وهو ميزان المصالح والمفاسد، ويُقدم الأصلح فالأصلح.

• الواجبات أكثر من الأوقات فإذا وجد الإنسان فراغا فليعلم أنها نعمة غُبن فيها كثير من الناس وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " نعمتان مغبون فيهما كثير من الناس الصحة والفراغ"

• ترشيد استغلال الوقت أبلغ من ترشيد استغلال المال ولذلك يحتاج المسلم من اجل ترشيد وقته إلى تخطيط وتنظيم؛ فالوقت المستغل استغلالا نافعا هو ما كان في أربعة امور:

1- الأمر الأول: علم يتعلمه، فالوقت الذي استغل في تعلم العلم الشرعي والعلوم النافعة وقت لم يخسر صاحبه، وقد سئل مالك عن المقرب للقتل الذي لم يبق من عمره إلا ساعة في أية طاعة يصرفها فقال: علم يتعلمه، قيل يا أبا عبد الله إنه لا يعمل به، قال تعلمه أفضل من العمل به...

2- الأمر الثاني: العمل بما تعلمه الإنسان ومبادرة فوات الأوان؛ فالمبادرة بالأعمال رشد كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " بادروا بالأعمال ستا فهل تنتظرون إلا غنى مطغيا أو فقرا منسيا ..." الحديث.

3- الأمر الثالث: الدعوة إلى ما تعلم وعمل به؛ ولا بد أن ينفق في سبيل ذلك وقتا وأن يقوم لله بالحق، فقد قال الله تعالي لرسوله: " قُلْ هَذِهِ سَبِيلِي أَدْعُو إِلَى اللَّهِ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنْ اتَّبَعَنِي وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَمَا أَنَا مِنْ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (108)(يوسف).

4- الأمر الرابع: الصبر على طريق الحق حتى يلق الله؛ وهذا زمان الصبر فلابد أن يحرص الإنسان على الصبر عن معصية الله والصبر على قدره، وقد قال الله تعالى: " إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ". وعليه أن يعلم أنه مفتون على هذا الطريق وأنه سيقتحم عقبات ونكبات لا بد منها، يصرف بها الله الذين لا يرتضي لهم خدمة هذا الدين ولا يرتضي سلوكهم للطريق المستقيم.

هذه جملة مقتطفات موجزة من محاضرة الشيخ في هذا الموضوع، وللاستماع لها كاملة اضغط هنا
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture — at the al-Huda Mosque in the Ksar district in the centre of the capital, Nouakchott — entitled "Making use of time in the life of the Muslim", after the sunset prayer on the evening of yesterday, Sunday. A large audience of students of knowledge and men of daʿwah attended, and there was a considerable attendance of women.

In his lecture the Sheikh took up the value of time in the life of the Muslim, and how a Muslim is to make use of his precious time in a way that accords with the many obligations laid upon him. In his talk the Sheikh set out for this a plan and an ordering that help a person to use his time wisely and to spend it on what is good and beneficial, guided in this by the jurisprudence of priorities and by the weighing of benefits (maṣāliḥ) against one another.

The lecture took up important topics — juristic, intellectual and admonitory. We mention the following of them in summary:

• Time is the capital, and a person cannot secure a profit once the capital is gone.

• The Qur'an magnified the matter of time: God, glorified and exalted, swore in more than one chapter by moments of time. He swore by the sun and the moon and their succession, and by the forenoon, and by the night, and by the day. All of this is an alerting to the importance of time and to its greatness.

• A person's time is his lifespan, and God made it unknown to him for a far-reaching underlying wisdom (ḥikmah) that none grasp but those of illumined minds.

• Time is an argument against a person, so he must hasten to put it to the best use. Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said: "A life whose beginning has been squandered is surely fit to have its end guarded."

• What remains of a lifespan is of great price, because it is by it that a person makes good what has passed. Muhammad ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-Wadud, may God Almighty have mercy on him, said:

*What is left of life is, in my reckoning, beyond price, even if tomorrow be an unloved portion of time; / in it a man makes good every chance lost out of time, and effaces the evil with the good.*

• To make the best use of his time a person needs to order his priorities and to consider which of them is best, and to hold back from acting in a matter until he knows God's ruling on what he is about to do. After that he hastens to comply with what is obligatory (wājib) among them; and when he has completed the obligatory he hastens to what completes the obligatory, namely the sunnah acts (sunan) and the recommended acts (mandūbāt); and when he reaches the level of the permissible (mubāḥ), he must weigh matters on another scale, the scale of benefits and harms (maṣāliḥ and mafāsid), giving precedence to what is more conducive to benefit, and then to what is next after it.

• The obligations are more numerous than the hours there are for them; so if a person finds himself with free time, let him know that it is a blessing in which many people are cheated. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Two blessings in which many people are cheated: health and free time."

• Using time wisely is weightier than using wealth wisely, and for that reason the Muslim needs planning and ordering in order to use his time wisely. Time put to beneficial use is time spent on four things:

1. The first: knowledge that he learns. Time spent in learning the Sharia sciences and the beneficial sciences is time in which the one who spent it has suffered no loss. Malik was asked about a man brought forward for execution, with only an hour of his life remaining: in what act of obedience should he spend it? He said: knowledge that he learns. It was said: O Abu ʿAbd Allah, he will not act upon it. He said: learning it is better than acting upon it…

2. The second: acting upon what one has learnt, and hastening before the time for it is gone. Hastening to deeds is right guidance, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Hasten to do good deeds ahead of six things. Are you waiting for anything but a wealth that makes you overstep, or a poverty that makes you forget…" — the rest of the report.

3. The third: calling others to what he has learnt and acted upon. He must spend time in that cause and stand for God in the truth, for God Almighty said to His Messenger: {Say: this is my way. I call to God upon clear insight, I and whoever follows me. And glory be to God, and I am not of those who associate partners with Him} (verse 108, Sūrat Yūsuf).

4. The fourth: patient endurance on the path of truth until he meets God. This is a time of patience, so a person must take care to be patient in keeping away from disobedience to God, and patient with His decree. God Almighty said: {The patient will be given their reward in full, without reckoning} [Sūrat al-Zumar 39:10]. And he must know that he is being tested on this road, and that he will have to force his way through obstacles and calamities that cannot be avoided, by which God turns away those for whom He does not approve the service of this religion, and whose treading of the straight path He does not approve.

These are a set of brief extracts from the Sheikh's lecture on this subject.

flags.arabic: هذه جملة مقتطفات موجزة من محاضرة الشيخ في هذا الموضوع، وللاستماع لها كاملة اضغط هنا
flags.context: the closing sentence of the record, and the status of everything above it
options: render with an excerpt banner and a link to the recording, never as a text by the Sheikh
flags.note: CRITICAL — critical_for_display. The record says in its own closing sentence that what precedes is a set of brief extracts, and that the lecture itself is audio. The bullets are the news desk's compression of an argument in legal theory, not the Sheikh's own wording, and the sixth bullet in particular reduces a graded scheme — obligatory, then the sunnah acts and the recommended, then the permissible weighed by benefit and harm — to four lines. A reader who meets this as an article will take a journalist's précis for the Sheikh's own exposition. The full lecture is the audio at /index.php/dawa/solok.html?view=media&id=1458.

flags.arabic: وقد قال الحسن بن أبي الحسن رحمه الله
flags.context: attribution of the saying 'a life whose beginning has been squandered…'
options: keep the name exactly as given: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan
render as al-Hasan al-Basri with the source form in brackets
flags.note: الحسن بن أبي الحسن is the patronymic of al-Hasan al-Basri and is how the classical sources often name him. The name is kept as the source gives it rather than replaced with the form an English reader would recognise; the identification is recorded here. A reviewer may prefer option 2 for a general readership, but that is an editorial decision, not a translator's.

flags.arabic: " إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ"
flags.context: the fourth of the four things time is well spent on
options: supply the locator in square brackets, as done here
give no locator at all, as the source gives none
give the locator without brackets, like the other two
flags.note: The source supplies locators for the two other scriptural quotations but none for this one, which is Sūrat al-Zumar 39:10. The style guide requires the reference format, so the locator is supplied — but in square brackets, so that it is visible as the translator's addition and not mistaken for something the source gave. The same treatment should be applied corpus-wide rather than settled here.

flags.arabic: " بادروا بالأعمال ستا فهل تنتظرون إلا غنى مطغيا أو فقرا منسيا ..." الحديث / " نعمتان مغبون فيهما كثير من الناس الصحة والفراغ"
flags.context: two prophetic reports cited in the lecture summary
options: translate and attribute exactly as given, with no collection and no grading
flags.note: Style guide section 4. No collection is named and no grading is given for either report, so the English supplies neither. Both could be sourced in a moment, but doing so would put a grading in the Sheikh's mouth that he did not give — and in any case these are the news desk's renderings of what he said, not his own citations. Note too that the first is abridged in the source itself, which closes it with الحديث ('the rest of the report'); the remaining five of the six things are not given.

flags.arabic: مسترشدا في ذلك بفقه الأولويات والموازنة بين المصالح
flags.context: the framework the lecture is said to have used
flags.note: فقه الأولويات is a twentieth-century term of art, not a classical category, and it is not in the glossary. 'The jurisprudence of priorities' is the established English rendering. Flagged because the term recurs across the corpus and should have one fixed form; option 3 would lose the fact that this is a named discipline.

translator_notes: This is a news report, and an avowedly abridged one. Everything attributed to the Sheikh arrives at second hand.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body places the lecture on the evening of 'yesterday, Sunday', which given the timestamp would be 3 July 2011; the day is given, the date is not, and it has not been supplied in the English.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The two lines of verse by Muhammad ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-Wadud are rendered as continuous prose in italics per style guide section 4, with / marking the break between the two lines. The source's hemistich markers (****) are kept in body_ar and not carried into the English. No rhymed English has been attempted.

The ruling words in the sixth bullet — الواجب، السنن، المندوبات، المباحات — are used of acts and take the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3. The kalām exemption of section 8 is not engaged anywhere in this record.

The source's closing clause 'to listen to it in full, click here' is the site's own navigation furniture; it is preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, and omitted from body_en. The sentence before it is not furniture but the source's own statement that this is an abridgement, and it is kept.
The oath verses alluded to in the second bullet (by the sun, the forenoon, the night, the day) are not quoted, so no locators are given for them.
